details:
Project Details

What it does & How it works: The Smart Farm Crop Rotation Recommender is an Arduino and LCD prototype for the "Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. It fuses NASA POWER 30-day climate baselines (rainfall 9.08mm, temp 27.84°C, soil wetness 0.795, humidity 81.99%) to guide seasonal planning. Two core functions: (1) Auto boot-time recommendation of 5 rotation strategies (Legume, Drought-tolerant, Cover Crop, Deep-root, Mixed); (2) Long-press button reveals raw NASA data for transparency. The device outputs trend-based advisories (not forecasts) on an LCD screen.

Benefits & Expected Impact: It offers low-cost, farmer-friendly access to satellite Earth observation, helping smallholders in Kuching, Sarawak adapt to climate variability and soil degradation. By protecting soil health through adaptive rotation, it supports climate-resilient agriculture while respecting local expertise. Expected impact: scalable, offline-ready decision support for small farms.

Tools, Language, Hardware: Developed with C++ (Arduino IDE), hardware includes Arduino board, LCD display, push button and more. NASA POWER API provides baseline data. Software: Arduino IDE, Google Sheets for data prep.

Innovation: Combines space agency data with ground sensing in a simple two-function interface; transparent "show source data" feature builds trust; trend-based logic avoids overclaiming as forecast.

Considerations: Designed for low-literacy/no-tech users (simple screen text); local climate context (Sarawak humid/moist); AI (SI) assisted code drafting and text with human-led design/validation; no NASA branding modified. AI used as innovation accelerator, not direct solution.
